The medical wound healing accelerator according to an embodiment of the present invention comprises: a body attachably and detachably provided on a fixing pin of an external fixator for fractures, the fixing pin being inserted into a bone through the skin; a plurality of light source units arranged on one lateral surface of the body so as to emit light toward the skin, the light providing a beneficial effect to a wound; and a controller electrically connected to the light source units to control the operation of the light source units. outputs.L2:
A device for accelerating medical wound healing is described. In one embodiment, the device includes a main body that can be removably attached to a fixing pin of an external fracture fixator, the fixing pin being inserted through the skin and into a bone. Multiple light source units are positioned on one side surface of the main body and are configured to direct light toward the skin, with the light producing a beneficial effect on the wound. The device also includes a controller that is electrically connected to the light source units and regulates their operation.

In addition, a device for treating osteomyelitis includes an insert that can be placed into an osteomyelitis-affected region inside the human body, along with multiple light-emitting elements mounted on the insert to radiate light. These light-emitting elements are arranged at intervals from one another along the longitudinal direction of the insert. The portion of the insert where the light-emitting elements are spaced apart may be cut or bent so that it conforms to the shape of the osteomyelitis-affected region.
outputs.L3:
A medical wound healing accelerator is designed for use with an external fracture fixator. The accelerator is configured to be attachably and detachably mounted on a fixing pin of the external fracture fixator, which is inserted through the skin and into a bone to stabilize a fractured area. By being mountable on the fixing pin, the device can be positioned close to the wound or pin insertion site without requiring a separate support structure, and it can be removed when treatment is complete or when access to the wound is needed.

The wound healing accelerator includes a body having one side on which a plurality of light source units are arranged. These light source units are positioned to emit light toward the patient’s skin, particularly toward the wound area or the region surrounding the fixing pin. The emitted light may be selected to provide a beneficial effect on wound healing, such as promoting tissue regeneration, reducing inflammation, improving local blood circulation, or assisting in sterilization depending on the wavelength and intensity used.

A controller is electrically connected to the plurality of light source units. The controller controls the operation of the light source units, including turning them on and off and, where applicable, adjusting treatment parameters such as irradiation time, light intensity, emission pattern, or wavelength. Through this controlled operation, the accelerator can provide consistent and targeted light treatment to the wound region while the external fracture fixator remains in place.

In addition to the wound healing accelerator, an osteomyelitis treatment device is provided for treating an osteomyelitis-affected area inside the human body. The osteomyelitis treatment device includes an insert configured to be placed into or near the affected area. The insert is designed to deliver therapeutic light directly to the infected or inflamed bone region, thereby supporting treatment of osteomyelitis from within or adjacent to the affected tissue.

The insert includes a plurality of light-emitting members arranged along its length at spaced intervals. This spacing allows light to be distributed over a wider treatment region rather than being concentrated at a single point. The insert may be cut to a desired length or bent into a desired shape so that it can conform to the size, contour, and position of the osteomyelitis-affected area. As a result, the device can be adapted to different anatomical locations and lesion shapes, enabling more effective and localized treatment.
outputs.L4:
A medical wound-healing accelerator and osteomyelitis treatment device are designed to deliver therapeutic light directly to injured, infected, or slow-healing tissue. The system includes attachable or insertable device bodies equipped with multiple controllable light-emitting units, such as LEDs or other medical light sources, arranged to irradiate a selected treatment area. By placing the light sources close to the affected tissue, the device can provide localized phototherapy intended to support tissue repair, reduce microbial activity, and improve the healing environment.

For external wound treatment, the device may be configured as an attachment that fits around or near an existing medical fixation structure, such as an external fixation pin used in orthopedic care. Because pin sites are prone to irritation, delayed healing, and infection, the light-emitting units can be positioned to direct light toward the surrounding skin and soft tissue. The device body may include openings, slots, or adjustable sections that allow it to be mounted around pins or other protruding medical components without interfering with their mechanical function. Multiple light-emitting units can be independently controlled so that different regions around the wound can receive different intensities, wavelengths, or exposure durations depending on clinical need.

For osteomyelitis treatment, the device may be formed as an insertable body that can be placed within or near an infected bone region. Osteomyelitis is a difficult-to-treat bone infection that often requires prolonged antibiotics, surgical debridement, and careful local management. By incorporating light-emitting units into a body that can be inserted into a bone cavity, surgical site, or infected region, the device can deliver therapeutic light directly to the area where infection and inflammation are present. This localized approach may improve treatment effectiveness by concentrating light energy at the site of disease rather than relying only on surface illumination.

The light-emitting units may be selected to emit one or more wavelengths associated with photobiomodulation, antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, or other therapeutic light-based mechanisms. For example, red or near-infrared light may be used to encourage cellular repair processes and improve local circulation, while blue or other selected wavelengths may be used for antimicrobial effects. In some embodiments, the device may also be used with a photosensitizing agent to enhance antimicrobial activity in infected tissue.

The system may include a controller for regulating the operation of each light-emitting unit. The controller can adjust parameters such as light intensity, wavelength, pulse pattern, treatment duration, and activation sequence. This allows treatment to be adapted to the size, depth, and condition of the wound or infected bone region. In some designs, the controller may operate preset treatment programs, while in others it may allow a clinician to customize therapy based on patient-specific requirements.

The device body may be made from biocompatible materials suitable for contact with tissue, bone, or surgical implants. For external applications, the body may be reusable or disposable and may include fastening structures to secure it in place during treatment. For insertable applications, the body may be shaped to fit into a bone defect or surgical cavity and may be designed for temporary placement, removal after treatment, or integration with other surgical components.

Overall, the designs provide a targeted and adaptable method for applying therapeutic light to wounds and osteomyelitis sites. By enabling controlled illumination around external fixation pins or directly within infected bone regions, the device may help accelerate wound healing, reduce infection risk, and support improved management of difficult orthopedic and soft-tissue conditions.

The word “the” is one of the most common and important words in English. It is a definite article, used to refer to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, in the phrase “the book,” the speaker is talking about a particular book, not just any book.

Additionally, words like “additionally” help connect ideas and make writing clearer. “Additionally” is used when adding more information to a sentence or paragraph. It helps show that one idea supports or expands on another.

Together, “the” and “additionally” may seem simple, but they play important roles in communication. “The” gives precision, while “additionally” creates smooth transitions between ideas. Using both correctly can make writing more organized, specific, and easy to understand.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a medical device that accelerates wound healing using light source units mounted on an external fixator pin, and also describe an osteomyelitis treatment insert with spaced light emitters that can be cut or bent to fit the infected area.
counterfactuals.output:
A medical treatment system is provided for promoting wound healing and treating infection at or near a bone fixation site. The system includes an external fixator pin configured for insertion into bone and one or more light source units mounted to, coupled with, or supported by the pin so as to direct therapeutic light toward surrounding soft tissue, a wound bed, a pin tract, or adjacent bone. The light source units may include LEDs, laser diodes, or other optical emitters selected to deliver one or more wavelengths, intensities, or pulsed illumination profiles effective to stimulate tissue repair, reduce inflammation, or inhibit microbial growth. Power and control circuitry may be carried by the fixator assembly or connected externally to regulate treatment duration, sequence, and output.

An osteomyelitis treatment insert is also disclosed. The insert comprises an elongate, flexible or formable carrier having a plurality of spaced light emitters disposed along its length for placement within, against, or adjacent to an infected bone region or debrided cavity. The carrier may be cut to a selected length and/or bent, curved, folded, or otherwise shaped to conform to the geometry of the infected area. The spaced emitters deliver antimicrobial or photobiomodulatory illumination to distributed portions of the treatment site, and may be encapsulated in a biocompatible, sterilizable, or resorbable material. The insert may be used alone or in combination with antibiotics, debridement, fixation hardware, or wound dressings to provide localized optical therapy for osteomyelitis and related wound conditions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention in formal patent language: a detachable wound healing accelerator for fracture external fixation pins that irradiates skin with therapeutic light, plus a flexible/cuttable light-emitting insert for treating osteomyelitis.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention relates generally to orthopedic fracture fixation and phototherapeutic wound management, and more particularly to a detachable light-therapy apparatus configured for use with external fixation pins and to a flexible implantable or insertable light-emitting member for treatment of infected bone or bone-adjacent tissue.

In one aspect, the invention provides a detachable wound-healing accelerator for use with an external fixation pin extending through a patient’s skin. The accelerator comprises a housing or body configured to be removably coupled to, supported by, or positioned around the external fixation pin adjacent a pin-skin interface. The body carries one or more therapeutic light emitters arranged to irradiate skin, soft tissue, and/or a pin tract surrounding the fixation pin. The emitted radiation may comprise, for example, red light, near-infrared light, blue light, ultraviolet light, or selected combinations thereof, at wavelengths, intensities, duty cycles, and exposure durations selected to promote wound healing, reduce inflammation, reduce microbial burden, stimulate local circulation, and/or decrease the incidence or severity of pin-site infection.

The device may include a central opening, slot, clamp, collar, split-ring structure, hinged member, resilient engagement feature, magnetic coupling, adhesive surface, or other detachable mounting arrangement permitting installation and removal without removing the external fixation pin. In certain embodiments, the light emitters are disposed circumferentially or partially circumferentially around the pin so as to deliver substantially uniform irradiation to tissue surrounding the pin entry site. The apparatus may further include a controller, power source, rechargeable battery, wired or wireless power interface, timing circuit, optical diffuser, reflector, heat-dissipation structure, sterile barrier, disposable cover, sensor, or communication module for regulating or monitoring treatment.

In another aspect, the invention provides a flexible light-emitting insert configured for placement in or adjacent infected bone, a medullary canal, a bone cavity, a debrided osteomyelitis site, or associated soft tissue. The insert comprises an elongate flexible substrate carrying one or more light-emitting elements, optical fibers, light guides, micro-LEDs, electroluminescent members, or other light-output structures configured to emit therapeutic radiation into surrounding tissue. The insert is bendable to conform to anatomical structures and may be cut to a selected length prior to or during use, while maintaining operability of at least a remaining portion of the light-emitting structure. The insert may be used to treat osteomyelitis by delivering antimicrobial, photobiomodulatory, photodynamic, or tissue-regenerative light energy directly to a target site.

In some embodiments, the flexible insert includes repeated electrical or optical segments, cut marks, sealed segment boundaries, parallel conductors, encapsulation layers, biocompatible polymer coatings, antimicrobial coatings, drug-eluting materials, radiopaque markers, fixation features, and/or connectors for coupling to an external or implanted power and control unit. The emitted light may be selected to activate a photosensitizer, reduce bacterial load, enhance bone regeneration, promote angiogenesis, or accelerate resolution of infection and inflammation.

Together, the detachable external pin-site accelerator and the flexible/cuttable light-emitting insert provide a modular therapeutic system for orthopedic infection control and wound healing, enabling noninvasive or minimally invasive delivery of controlled therapeutic light to both external fixation pin tracts and internal osteomyelitis treatment sites.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

1. A medical wound healing accelerator comprising:  
a body configured to be detachably attached to a fixing pin inserted into or positioned adjacent to a wound region of a patient;  
a plurality of light sources disposed on or in the body and configured to emit therapeutic light toward tissue surrounding the fixing pin; and  
a controller operatively connected to the plurality of light sources,  
wherein the controller is configured to control at least one of an emission wavelength, emission intensity, emission duration, emission interval, and emission sequence of the plurality of light sources so as to accelerate healing of the wound region.

2. The medical wound healing accelerator of claim 1, wherein the body includes a coupling portion configured to engage an external circumferential surface of the fixing pin.

3. The medical wound healing accelerator of claim 1, wherein the plurality of light sources are arranged circumferentially around the fixing pin when the body is attached to the fixing pin.

4. The medical wound healing accelerator of claim 1, wherein the plurality of light sources include at least one light-emitting diode configured to emit light in a red or near-infrared wavelength range.

5. The medical wound healing accelerator of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to selectively drive different ones of the plurality of light sources according to a preset irradiation pattern.

6. The medical wound healing accelerator of claim 1, further comprising a power supply accommodated in the body or electrically connectable to the body.

7. The medical wound healing accelerator of claim 1, wherein the body is formed to be attachable to and detachable from the fixing pin without removal of the fixing pin from the patient.

8. An osteomyelitis treatment device comprising:  
an elongated support member configured to be inserted into a bone or a medullary canal;  
a plurality of light-emitting members provided along a longitudinal direction of the elongated support member and spaced apart from one another; and  
a controller configured to supply driving power to the plurality of light-emitting members,  
wherein the plurality of light-emitting members are configured to emit therapeutic light at respective positions spaced in the longitudinal direction to irradiate bone tissue affected by osteomyelitis.

9. The osteomyelitis treatment device of claim 8, wherein the plurality of light-emitting members are arranged at predetermined intervals along the elongated support member.

10. The osteomyelitis treatment device of claim 8, wherein each of the plurality of light-emitting members includes one or more light-emitting diodes configured to emit red light, near-infrared light, ultraviolet light, or a combination thereof.

11. The osteomyelitis treatment device of claim 8, wherein the controller is configured to independently control the plurality of light-emitting members.

12. The osteomyelitis treatment device of claim 8, wherein the elongated support member includes an internal passage through which an electrical conductor extends to electrically connect the controller to the plurality of light-emitting members.

13. The osteomyelitis treatment device of claim 8, wherein the elongated support member is configured as a pin, rod, nail, screw, or catheter insertable into a bone region.

14. The osteomyelitis treatment device of claim 8, wherein the plurality of light-emitting members are exposed through or covered by a light-transmissive portion of the elongated support member.

15. A medical light treatment system comprising:  
the medical wound healing accelerator of claim 1; and  
the osteomyelitis treatment device of claim 8,  
wherein the controller of the medical wound healing accelerator and the controller of the osteomyelitis treatment device are configured to provide controlled light irradiation to external wound tissue and internal bone tissue, respectively.

A wound-healing accelerator attached to an external fixator pin, and an osteomyelitis treatment device, are disclosed.

The wound-healing accelerator, which is attached to an external fixator pin inserted into a patient’s bone through the patient’s skin, comprises: a holder configured to receive the external fixator pin; a pad mounted on one side of the holder and configured to come into contact with a wound around the external fixator pin; and a light-emitting portion provided on the pad and configured to emit light toward the wound.
